The Sikandar page has him 'expanded Lodi rule into the regions of Gwalior and Bihar' and the Lodi page 'conquest and annexation of Bihar from the Sharqis', both undated; the Jaunpur page dates the end: 'In 1494, Sultan Hussain Shah Sharqi was defeated' at Benares (it names Bahlul, who the Bahlul page has dead in 1489). Cliopatria's Lodi step is 1497; 1494 is the page's year (repair 2026-10-20: was a confidence-1 event of 1497 naming a Jaunpur that ended in 1479). The land is the Sharqi rump inside the 1497 shape; the Bihar block west of Barh is gained from Bengal in 1496.

ledger.note: 1496: the Barh treaty. 'Sikandar Lodi halted the advance of his army and concluded a treaty of friendship with Ala-ud-din Husain Shah. According to this agreement, the country west of Barh went to Sikandar Lodi' and 'the country east of Barh remained under Husain Shah'. Barh is on the south bank of the Ganges at 25.48 N 85.72 E. The region is cut to the south bank (Patna, Gaya) because the page also has Husain Shah in 'firm control' of the trans-Gandak country in 1501-1502. Mirrors sultanate-of-bengal (1496 loss).
1496: the treaty ends the campaign (see the 1496 gain).

region.text: the rest of Cliopatria's 1497 step outside the old Sharqi realm and the Gwalior country (about 140 cells between 77.4 and 84.6 E)

ledger.note: 1497: Cliopatria's Lodi step adds about 418 cells; the Sharqi rump (1494 gain) and the Gwalior country (taken only in 1518, removed in the keyframe) account for part. The rest, about 140 cells between 77.4 and 84.6 E and 24.8 and 29.7 N, has no page: the Sikandar page says only 'He expanded Lodi rule into the regions of Gwalior and Bihar' (undated). Bridge at confidence 1 so that the keyframe step has an event (repair 2026-10-20).
1500: punitive expedition against Gwalior. 'He launched a punitive expedition against Gwalior after its ruler gave asylum to rebels from Delhi.'
1501: Dholpur taken. 'he captured Dholpur, a dependency of Gwalior.' (Mandrayal fort 1504; Uditnagar February 1507.)

c. 1505: the court moves to Agra. Sikandar 'commissioned the building of the present-day city of Agra' in 1503 and 'Sometime later ... moved his base' there; the Lodi page says he re-founded it in 1504. The move is undated on both.
December 1508: Narwar taken. 'He besieged Narwar for about a year before capturing it. In December 1508 he placed it under Raj Singh Kachchwaha.'

1517: Jalal Khan's revolt. Ibrahim 'took the throne and defeated his brother Jalaluddin, who had raised Pashtun nobles against him in Jaunpur'; Ibrahim had made Jalal governor of Jaunpur and Jalal asserted independence.
1517: Jalal Khan beaten 'by the end of the year' (he fled to Kalpi, then Gwalior, Malwa and the Gonds, and was captured and executed).
1518: Gwalior taken. 'After the fall of the Gwalior and taking control of its fortress in 1518'; Vikramaditya Tomar surrendered.
1518: the Gwalior campaigns of 1500-1518 end with the fortress's surrender.

region.text: the eastern provinces, read as Bihar

ledger.note: The eastern provinces secede. After Darya Khan Lohani died, 'his son Bahar Khan declared independence in the eastern provinces', joined by Nasir Khan Lohani, Fath Khan and Sher Khan Sur; the page gives no year and does not name Bihar. 1519 is Cliopatria's step.

region.text: the lands up to the Tons river: Lodi's 1497 holdings between 83.2 E and 85 E (Bihar west of Bengal's block to Azamgarh)

ledger.note: c. 1523: Nasrat Shah annexes the lands up to the Tons river: 'annexed the lands up to Tons river soon after 1522', after 'the collapse of the Lodi authority in Bihar' and 'entering into an alliance with the Lohani rebels' (Nasrat page). Mirrors sultanate-of-bengal (1523 gain). Much of this land is already out of the 1519 correction (Bihar, lost to Bahar Khan Lohani, /ledger 1519); the part still Lodi's is the strip between Bihar's west edge and the Tons.

region.text: Lahore, Jhelum, Sialkot, Kalanaur and Dipalpur

ledger.note: 1524: Babur takes the Punjab. 'Babur reached Lahore ... The Lodi army marched out to engage Babur and was routed'; he also took Jhelum, Sialkot, Kalanaur and Dipalpur before returning to Kabul (Ibrahim page: 'took control of the Punjab'). Babur's Kabul realm sits in the Timurid row.

21 April 1526: Babur wins at Panipat. 'The battle of Panipat was militarily a decisive victory for Babur'; 'Ibrahim and 20,000 of his men were killed in the battle'; the Delhi Sultanate 'annexed by the Mughal dynasty'. Mahmud Lodi fought on to Ghaghra in 1529 without a state.

wars.name: Lodi invasion of Bengal
wars.outcome: Sikandar Lodi's expedition of 1496 met the Bengal army at Barh; a treaty of friendship gave the country west of Barh to Lodi and left the country east of Barh with Husain Shah.

wars.name: Sikandar Lodi's Gwalior campaigns
wars.outcome: Dholpur 1501, Mandrayal 1504, Uditnagar 1507, Narwar 1508; the siege of Gwalior fort failed in 1505-1506; Ibrahim Lodi took Gwalior in 1518.

wars.name: Jalal Khan's revolt
wars.outcome: Ibrahim's brother, made governor of Jaunpur, asserted independence; defeated by the end of 1517 after Azam Humayun Sarwani defected.

wars.name: Ibrahim Lodi's war with Rana Sanga
wars.outcome: The page: 'Ibrahim sent another army against Rana Sanga of Mewar and was defeated' (year 1518 given only as the year of the Gwalior fall); no border change is recorded on the page.
wars.note: The page does not mention Khatoli, Dholpur or Chanderi.

wars.name: First Battle of Panipat
wars.outcome: Babur took Lahore and the Punjab towns in 1524 and defeated and killed Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat on 21 April 1526.

certainty.note: The one dated frontier is the Barh treaty of 1496 with Alauddin Hussain Shah ('the country west of Barh went to Sikandar Lodi', Alauddin Hussain Shah page), given in words, not as a line, and contradicted by the page's own 1501-1502 inscription across the Gandak, so it stays soft. The Doab, Bihar and Gwalior frontiers are approximate. (Repair 2026-10-20: the earlier note called the treaty undated.)

notes:
Cliopatria rows: one, 1453-1528, seven shapes. The page has the dynasty from 19 April 1451 (new 1451 keyframe) to Panipat on 21 April 1526 (1527-1528 dropped). Cliopatria's Mughal row starts in 1529; Babur's Kabul realm is in its Timurid row, hence the Punjab loss of 1524 names timurid-empire and the end names mughal-empire.
Shape problems: Jaunpur's land is added in 1482 against the page's 1479; the 1497 shape holds Gwalior (taken 1518 per the Ibrahim page) and has no dated Bihar conquest; the 1519 shape drops 195k km2 of the east that the pages do not show lost (only Bahar Khan's 'eastern provinces', undated, and Jalal Khan's revolt beaten in 1517); the 1526 shape keeps Lahore, taken in 1524. The corrections keep Awadh, Jaunpur, Allahabad and Kannauj with the Lodis to 1526 on the strength of the pages' silence: this is a reading (confidence 1-2) a gap-filler should test against the Mughal and Bihar dossiers.
Pages disagree: the Jaunpur page has 'Bahlul' defeating Hussain Shah at Benares in 1494 although the Bahlul Lodi page has him dying in July 1489 (Sikandar was sultan); Agra founded 1503 (Sikandar page) or 1504 (Lodi page); the Lodi page puts Sikandar's accession on 17 July 1489 (death date) or 15 July (crowning); Panipat on 20 or 21 April 1526 on the Ibrahim page.
Not on the pages opened: Tirhut, Chanderi, Bayana, Sambhal, Etawah, the Bengal treaty's date, Dilawar Khan, Alam Khan's role, Khatoli and Dholpur 1518-1519, and any area figure. Page budget (5) used: Lodi dynasty, Bahlul Lodi, Sikandar Lodi, Ibrahim Lodi, First Battle of Panipat.
Counterparts: 'Tomars of Gwalior', 'ruler of Narwar', 'Jalal Khan', 'Bahar Khan Lohani' are the pages' own terms, not dossiers; the Rajput dossiers (kingdom-of-mewar) exist. Gazetteer: Dholpur, Narwar, Dipalpur, Kalanaur, Jhelum are not in the gazetteer (lon/lat or nearby cities used).

Repair 2026-10-20 (reviewer sa-04-c): agreed with jaunpur-sultanate and sultanate-of-bengal. Jaunpur now runs to 1494 (rump in the east), so the 1479 gain is the core only and the east is gained in 1494 (Jaunpur page, defeat at Benares), not in Cliopatria's 1497; the rest of the 1497 step is a confidence-1 bridge. Added: the 1457 gain of Shamsabad; the 1496 campaign against Bengal and the Barh treaty (gain of the south-bank country west of Barh, from Bengal, with the war and its certainty note); the loss of the lands up to the Tons river to Nasrat Shah, c. 1523 (Nasrat page). The Bihar block was never in Lodi's Cliopatria shapes, so no 1482 loss exists; Bengal's 1482 gain names the Sharqi rump. The 1497 to 1526 keyframes are split at 1494, 1496, 1518, 1523 and 1524 so that each event shows in the shapes. Still open: Bahar Khan Lohani's year and extent, the move to Agra, and the eastern territory of 1519-1526 (kept on the pages' silence).
